subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: What explicit contract should distinguish an accepted non-zero exec outcome from a genuine normally terminated command failure for user-facing warnings?
rationale: The runtime’s `completed` state only means the process terminated normally; choosing whether to add accepted-exit metadata, alter notification policy, or retain all non-zero warnings is a product contract that source inspection cannot decide safely.

options.title: Require explicit accepted-exit metadata
options.body: Preserve non-zero warnings by default and suppress them only when the exec result carries an invocation-specific semantic-success signal.

options.title: Suppress every normal non-zero exit
options.body: Accept that channel users will no longer receive failure warnings for any process that exits normally with a non-zero code.

options.title: Keep current warning behavior
options.body: Close this PR and continue treating every finite non-zero exec code as an error until a narrower contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Require explicit accepted-exit metadata
recommendation.body: Preserve non-zero warnings by default and suppress them only when the exec result carries an invocation-specific semantic-success signal.
